memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you. Do this at the appointed time in the month of Aviv, for in that month you came out of Egypt.'" - Exod 34:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God builds remembering into Israel's calendar. Every year, at a fixed time, they would stop and eat bread without yeast — bread made in a hurry, the bread of people leaving in the night.

Why? Because we forget. We forget quickly and thoroughly, and Israel had just demonstrated it at the foot of Sinai. So God gave them a rhythm of remembering that did not depend on how they happened to feel.

This is deeply practical wisdom. Our faith needs habits, not just moments. Regular Bible reading, weekly gathering with God's people, spoken thanksgiving at meals, marking anniversaries of God's kindness — these are not empty rituals. They are how truth gets into us over years.

Jesus gave His church exactly this kind of remembering. Taking bread, He said, "do this in remembrance of me" (Luke 22:19). Not because we might forget the facts, but because we so easily forget what they cost and what they mean.

And every Passover pointed forward. Paul says plainly: "Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed" (1 Cor 5:7). The festival Israel kept for centuries found its meaning at Calvary.

What rhythms of remembering have you built into your life?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What habits help you remember what God has done?
2. Do your spiritual practices depend on how you feel that day?
3. How does the Lord's Supper deepen your grasp of the gospel?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I forget so easily. Build into my life rhythms that keep Your goodness before my eyes. Amen.
